newsitem.title: USA: Rubin intervention remarks don't faze dlr bulls.
newsitem.headline: Rubin intervention remarks don't faze dlr bulls.

text.p: The dollar's jump after Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin on Monday said the U.S. would intervene only when appropriate was not a response to any perceived change in dollar policy, traders said.
"I think (Rubin's statement) has little to do with the market movement; it is as expected," said Russell LaScala, head of spot dealing at Citibank.
Dollar/mark jumped to a new 37-month high at 1.73 shortly after Rubin's comments, but traders said the rise was fueled by overall bullishness and a rebound in U.S. assets.

Meanwhile, the dollar was largely static against the yen after Rubin said U.S. policy was unchanged when asked about possible U.S./Japan intervention to prop up the crumbling yen. He added: "We'll act when it's appropriate and not act when it's not appropriate."
Traders said the dollar seemed poised to continue rallying until it encounters intervention. But only the Bank of Japan seems sufficiently worried to act soon.
"The market is going to go until they see the whites of their eyes, until they see intervention," said Bob Near, a vice president at Bank of New York.
"I think this thing will end in intervention and the first line will be the Bank of Japan," said Near.

The dollar garnered support after the Dow Jones industrials repaired early Monday losses to post a 50-point gain during the afternoon. The Treasury bond market also trimmed modest declines to stand nearly flat late in the day.

At 1600 EDT/2000 GMT the dollar was at 1.7305/15 marks, up from 1.7210/20 at the open and near 1.7240 before Rubin's remarks. Versus the yen, it was at 126.58/68, up from an open of 126.13/23 yen and slightly above 126.35 yen before the Treasury Secretary spoke. (( -- 212-859-1667 ))
